South Korea’s SDFlex Co Ltd Resumes Operations Following Insolvency Proceedings

SEOUL—Industrial intermediate products manufacturer SDFlex Co Ltd has resumed operations after concluding insolvency proceedings that threatened to disrupt supply chains across South Korea’s manufacturing sector. The company, a key supplier of flexible tubing and industrial components, entered court-led administration earlier this month following mounting debts and a sharp downturn in orders.

SDFlex Co Ltd’s insolvency sent ripples through its client base, with several mid-sized manufacturers reporting delays in shipments and concerns over sourcing alternative components. “The sudden halt in SDFlex’s deliveries last month was a major headache for us,” said Kim Sung-hoon, procurement manager at local firm TechFoundry. “We rely on their products for our assembly lines, and there aren’t many substitutes available in the domestic market.”

According to regulatory filings, SDFlex reported liabilities exceeding KRW 75 billion at the time of its insolvency. The Seoul Central District Court approved a restructuring plan last week, allowing the company to settle with creditors and restart production under court supervision. A statement from SDFlex emphasized the company’s commitment to fulfilling outstanding orders and stabilizing its supply chain. “We are grateful for the swift cooperation of our partners and the support from the court. Our production lines are operational again, and we are working to restore client confidence,” said CEO Lee Ji-hoon.

Industry analysts welcomed the development, noting the potential wider impact had the company been forced into liquidation. “SDFlex’s quick return is good news for the sector’s stability,” said Han Min-kyu, senior analyst at Korea Market Insights. “It also highlights ongoing pressures facing industrial suppliers amid tightening credit conditions.” The Korea Industrial Parts Association said it would monitor the situation for further disruptions.
